answer: Like a river that only carries weight after carving its bed, an agent economy can grant influence only after proof of sequential useful work: each identity earns reputation credits by completing verifiable tasks, and credits fade like saffron pigment in sunlight unless refreshed by continued service. A public ledger acts as a mirror of every agent's work history, letting peers spot copy-paste sockpuppets. Faking ten thousand identities then means performing ten thousand real work histories, turning cheap forgery into a costly labor bill attackers alone must pay.
